examples.solution_text:
Multiply each component by the scalar.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-\frac{3}{5}\begin{pmatrix}10\\-15\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}(-\frac{3}{5})(10)\\(-\frac{3}{5})(-15)\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}-6\\9\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}$

From tail to tip, move 3 units right and 2 units down.
$\underset{\sim}{a}=\begin{pmatrix}3\\-2\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{aligned}-2\underset{\sim}{a}&=-2\begin{pmatrix}3\\-2\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}(-2)(3)\\(-2)(-2)\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}-6\\4\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}$

The vector $\underset{\sim}{w}$ is half as long as $\underset{\sim}{v}$ and points in the opposite direction. The scalar is therefore negative.
$\underset{\sim}{w}=-\frac{1}{2}\underset{\sim}{v}$

Equate corresponding components and divide by the scalar.
$\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{3}x&=10\\x&=10\div\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right)\\x&=-6\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{3}y&=-15\\y&=-15\div\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right)\\y&=9\end{aligned}$

Use the first component to find the scalar, then apply it to the second component.
$\begin{aligned}-6k&=15\\k&=-\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}h&=\left(-\frac{5}{2}\right)(4)\\h&=-10\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: Component multiplication gives (-3/5)(10)=-6 and (-3/5)(-15)=9, so the resultant column vector is (-6,9). The method matches the scalar rule and fractional-scalar activities at source lines 1203–1214 and 1247–1256.
The arrow from (1,3) to (4,1) has displacement (3,-2). Multiplying both components by -2 gives (-6,4). Reading tail-to-tip displacement and then scaling matches source lines 988–1008 and 1137–1214.

The diagram gives v=(4,2) and w=(-2,-1). Thus w=-v/2: its length is half that of v and its direction is opposite. Source Foundation question 1, lines 748–766 and attached image 11, supports identifying signed scalar multiples geometrically.

The given arrow has displacement (4,2). The solution arrows have displacements (6,3) and (-2,-1), respectively 3a/2 and -a/2. The point correctly represents 0a, with zero magnitude and no direction. Attached image 8 and source lines 423–428, 511–557 and 736–743 support these constructions. Derived arrows appear only in the solution.
Distributing -3/4 gives (-3/4)(8)i+(-3/4)(-12)j=-6i+9j. This follows the component-form multiplication method at source lines 1956–1962.
Equating components gives -5x/3=10 and -5y/3=-15. Dividing by -5/3 yields x=-6 and y=9; substitution reproduces both resultant components. This adapts source Foundation question 3, lines 1325–1333.

The first component gives -6k=15, hence k=-5/2. The second gives h=4k=-10. Component matching is supported by source lines 1203–1214, 1325–1333 and 1739–1753, without introducing a parallelism assessment.
